lines.text: Every earthquake on Earth, in about a hundred and ten years, adds up to less than one magnitude ten.
There are about half a million detectable earthquakes a year. Pour all of them in.
The total comes to the equivalent of one magnitude nine point nine five.
And the line it falls short of is a quake no known fault can produce.
Now the strange part. One single earthquake is somewhere between a tenth and a fifth of that entire total.
So which one was it? And could a ten ever happen? That's in the full video, linked right here.
